name: DCB Bank Ltd
title: DCB Bank Ltd - 532772 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: DCB Bank Q1 FY27 PAT rose 36% to INR 213 crores, a record quarter, with cost-to-average assets at a historic low of 2.42%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly PAT of INR 213 crores (up 36% YoY) and EPS of 6.62, with ROE of 13.61%. Deposits grew 20.06% YoY and advances 17.06% YoY, with NIM at 3.35% (up 15 bps YoY). Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 2.43% and NNPA at 0.84%, while a one-time treasury gain of INR 101 crores in Q1 FY26 (only INR 16 crores this year) was offset by core fee growth of 31% to INR 175 crores. Management reiterated the FY27 ROE guidance of 13.5% and FY28 of 14.5%, and said cost-to-average assets should stay below 2.5%.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loans drove the Q1 product mix and carry lower yield and cost; management caps LTV at 75% for internal sourcing versus RBI's 85%. Gold is expected to settle at 20-22% of the book; gold NPA stock is about INR 20-30 crores on a book of roughly INR 7,000-7,500 crores.

segments.name: Mortgages (home loans and LAP)
segments.commentary: Disbursements of INR 1,500 crores were up 35% YoY from INR 1,100 crores. Mortgage book is about INR 29,000 crores, growing about 10% YoY and 1% QoQ, with the DA book run down and now fully organic sourcing. Business loan to home loan mix is about 70/30.

segments.name: MSME / SME
segments.commentary: SME book is about INR 1,800 crores, and MSME disbursements have fallen YoY for several quarters. Management is focused on current accounts (CA growth of 5% YoY), MSME overdrafts and trade finance, with improvement targeted for Q2 and Q3.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Run-down legacy book of about INR 350 crores with no fresh sourcing; the team has been wound down.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Management guides co-lending to stay below 15% of the book and expects about 13-14%. Co-lending grew slower this quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ROE of 13.5% and FY28 ROE of 14.5%, with management saying this should come without a hockey-stick move.
Cost to average assets to stay below the 2.5% guidance, with the full year around 2.45%; headcount may rise from about 11,500 toward 13,000.
NIM expected to rise in Q2 and beyond, driven by a 7-8% decline in cost of deposits (14 bps in Q1) and higher-yield mortgage and agri mix; the one-day extra in Q1 (91 vs 90 days) is a minor impact.
Around 20 new branches this year, taking the network to about 500; growth will rely more on people than branches.
ECL goes live in April 2027; the floating provision of INR 210 crores is seen as adequate buffer, with INR 6-7 crores added each quarter.

Management said it is open to capital raising over the next three years, with an AGM-approved enabling resolution for up to INR 2,000 crores (including INR 1,500 crores of Tier 1). Timing, size and pricing rest with the board.
capex_capacity: Branch network targeted at about 500 by year-end, adding about 20 branches, mostly second or third branches in existing cities.
Headcount at 11,554, down from 11,896 in June 2024; business per employee at INR 11.06 crores.
Continued investment in technology and AI; the call did not detail capex amounts.
Capital raising enabling resolution for up to INR 2,000 crores; no timing decided.
demand_pricing: Mortgage disbursements up 35% YoY, but growth lags because the DA book is being run down; management expects a 22-23% growth path if disbursements keep rising 30-35%.
Gold loan prices fell from about INR 17,000 per gram mid-quarter to INR 14,400; the 75% LTV cap avoided margin calls.
Management says it sees no pricing pressure in gold loans from PSU banks, while noting that peers offer up to 85% LTV.
Management says loan demand is strong and it can choose customers; it sees no stress in service-sector MSMEs from tariffs or inflation.

Deposit pricing: fresh deposits are being sourced at lower rates than before, and the bank is no longer one of the highest-paying banks; cost of deposits over five quarters went 7.12%, 6.96%, 6.86%, 6.84%, 6.71%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did yield on advances fall 23 bps QoQ, and how will yields, funding costs and NIM move?
qa_highlights.answer: Yield fell to 10.75% on gold-heavy mix; mortgage and secured non-gold mix should lift yields over Q2-Q4. Mix target is about 70/30 business to home loans. NIM improvement is expected to come mainly from lower cost of funds.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fee income decline QoQ and is this seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 has higher third-party distribution and processing fees; Q1 is seasonally weaker. Core fee income is up 31% YoY, and management says Q4-to-Q1 decline was smaller than last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why is MSME disbursement falling YoY, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus on current accounts (5% YoY growth), MSME overdrafts and trade finance; TReDS was stopped as low-yield. New people and sectors added, with output expected in Q2 and clearer gains in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining deposit repricing, and is cost of funds bottoming?
qa_highlights.answer: Some repricing tail remains into Q2. Cost of deposits fell 14 bps in Q1, with 7-8% further decline expected. Management says fresh deposits are also being priced lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mortgage growth slower, and was it a choice to protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was not a margin choice; the DA book was stopped about a year ago and is running down. Disbursements are up 35% YoY and foreclosures are not rising.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CD ratio rise and what is the outlook on co-lending?
qa_highlights.answer: CD ratio is 80.49%; asset growth may outpace liabilities. Co-lending is capped at 15% and is expected at about 13-14%; organic lending is the priority.

qa_highlights.question: Does the bank see stress from crude prices, war or inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact so far. Non-gold slippage is 1.52%, bounce ratios are low and credit bureau data show no problem in its ticket-size segments.

risks_watch: MSME disbursement and current account traction must improve in Q2-Q3; trade finance and CASA (21.65%, CA growth 5%) remain weak points.
Fee income is cyclical: treasury income was INR 16 crores this quarter versus INR 101 crores last year, and core fee income is seasonal.
Gold loan book growth is near 100% YoY; price volatility and a possible competitive loosening of the 75% LTV cap are watch items.
ECL implementation from April 2027 could add provisioning pressure; the floating provision buffer is INR 210 crores.
The CEO's tenure runs to April 2027; the board has not yet discussed extension.
Yield on advances fell 23 bps QoQ; NIM expansion depends on cost-of-deposit cuts and mortgage mix shifts.
summary.management_tone: Confident and consistent on delivered guidance (cost, GNPA, NNPA, ROE), with the CEO repeatedly tying credibility to past delivery. He was more cautious and somewhat evasive on mortgage growth timing, MSME recovery and the capital raise, which he said has no urgency.
key_quotes: So despite CASA declining, we are seeing that our cost -of-deposit, cost-of-funds actually has come down from 7.18 to 6.75.
So we were very clear that even if it means that you have a higher carrying cost, it is important to get money now than money later.
An ROE of 13.5% in this year should happen without a hockey stick kind of movement.

adds.what: About 20 new branches in existing cities, taking network to about 500 by year-end

growth.why: Management guides FY27 ROE of 13.5% and FY28 ROE of 14.5% without a hockey-stick move, backed by ~20 new branches (to ~500), 17% advance growth and 20% deposit growth, though no revenue growth figure was given and the treasury income drop offsets core fee growth.
